digest.component_or_area: jira data center adapter transport layer
propositions: A Python transport for Jira Data Center must satisfy TicketTransport plus SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, and SupportsAbsenceProbe roles, built on pycontribs/jira rather than a hand-rolled client and confined to an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra to preserve engine dependency-free contract.
The transport must unwrap the library's object model at the boundary, returning raw payload shapes that existing mappers consume, never exposing jira.Issue objects downstream.

TLS certificate verification must never be disabled; the transport must reject non-https base_url with ConfigError unless allow_insecure=true, and verification failures must name the ca_bundle setting rather than silently proceeding.

The resolved_statuses config must be configurable since self-hosted DC workflows can name resolved states differently than Cloud/DIG defaults (Resolved, Done, Cancelled); hardcoded names would misclassify resolved issues as PRESENT_FILTERED.

Every TicketTransport and Supports* method must have passing live test coverage against the J5 harness, including methods previously untested (add_label, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, map_remote_links, link_payload_for_relation) which revealed a production bug in label operations.

HTTP errors must not be retried (exactly one attempt), while connection timeouts and socket-layer read timeouts must be retried with documented backoff, and the DC backend must self-register into _backend_registry so select_backend('jira-datacenter') resolves after importing adapters.
